title: Rigveda 9.83: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.83: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.83 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 710r-710v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.83.1-5 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 3, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 710v
translation.original_text:
1pa̱vitra̍ṁ te̱ vita̍tam brahmaṇas pate pra̱bhur gātrā̍ṇi̱ pary e̍ṣi vi̱śvata̍ḥ | ata̍ptatanū̱r na tad ā̱mo a̍śnute śṛ̱tāsa̱ id vaha̍nta̱s tat sam ā̍śata ||
2tapo̍ṣ pa̱vitra̱ṁ vita̍taṁ di̱vas pa̱de śoca̍nto asya̱ tanta̍vo̱ vy a̍sthiran | ava̍nty asya pavī̱tāra̍m ā̱śavo̍ di̱vas pṛ̱ṣṭham adhi̍ tiṣṭhanti̱ ceta̍sā ||
3arū̍rucad u̱ṣasa̱ḥ pṛśni̍r agri̱ya u̱kṣā bi̍bharti̱ bhuva̍nāni vāja̱yuḥ | mā̱yā̱vino̍ mamire asya mā̱yayā̍ nṛ̱cakṣa̍saḥ pi̱taro̱ garbha̱m ā da̍dhuḥ ||
4ga̱ndha̱rva i̱tthā pa̱dam a̍sya rakṣati̱ pāti̍ de̱vānā̱ṁ jani̍mā̱ny adbhu̍taḥ | gṛ̱bhṇāti̍ ri̱puṁ ni̱dhayā̍ ni̱dhāpa̍tiḥ su̱kṛtta̍mā̱ madhu̍no bha̱kṣam ā̍śata ||
5ha̱vir ha̍viṣmo̱ mahi̱ sadma̱ daivya̱ṁ nabho̱ vasā̍na̱ḥ pari̍ yāsy adhva̱ram | rājā̍ pa̱vitra̍ratho̱ vāja̱m āru̍haḥ sa̱hasra̍bhṛṣṭir jayasi̱ śravo̍ bṛ̱hat ||
translation.text:
1SPREAD is thy cleansing filter, Brahmaṇaspati: as Prince, thou enterest its limbs from every side. The raw, whose mass hath not been heated gains not this: they only which are dressed, which bear, attain to it.
2High in the seat of heaven is spread the Scorcher's sieve: its threads are standing separate, glittering with light. The Swift Ones favour him who purifieth this: with consciousness they stand upon the height of heaven.
3The foremost spotted Steer hath made the Mornings shine, and yearning after strength sustains all things that be. By his high wisdom have the mighty Sages wrought: the Fathers who behold mankind laid down the germ,
4Gandharva verily protects his dwellingplace; Wondrous, he guards the generations of the Gods. Lord of the snare, he takes the foeman with the snare: those who are most devout have gained a share of meath.
5Rich in oblations! robed in cloud, thou corapassest oblation, sacrifice, the mighty seat of Gods. King, on thy chariot-sieve thou goest up to war, and with a thousand weapons winnest lofty fame.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 710v (numbered 27v by the scribe) (OPenn image 711, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.83.1 ‹-vi-tatam brahmaṇaḥ pate pra-bhuḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 711r (numbered 28r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.84.1 ‹vāyave kṛdhi naḥ adya›. Verses 9.83.1-5 end on this page; 9.83.1 begins on fol. 710r (numbered 27r by the scribe).
